005package org.wpilib.system;
006
007import static org.wpilib.units.Units.Seconds;
008
009import org.wpilib.driverstation.MatchState;
010import org.wpilib.units.measure.Time;
011
012/**
013 * A timer class.
014 *
015 * <p>Note that if the user calls SimHooks.restartTiming(), they should also reset the timer so
016 * get() won't return a negative duration.
017 */
018public class Timer {
019  /**
020   * Return the clock time in seconds. By default, the time is the time returned by
021   * getMonotonicTimestamp(). However, the return value of this method may be modified to use any
022   * time base, including non-monotonic time bases.
023   *
024   * @return Robot running time in seconds.
025   */
026  public static double getTimestamp() {
027    return RobotController.getTime() / 1_000_000_000.0;
028  }
029
030  /**
031   * Return the monotonic clock time in seconds.
032   *
033   * @return Monotonic time in seconds.
034   */
035  public static double getMonotonicTimestamp() {
036    return RobotController.getMonotonicTime() / 1_000_000_000.0;
037  }
038
039  /**
040   * Return the approximate match time. The FMS does not send an official match time to the robots,
041   * but does send an approximate match time. The value will count down the time remaining in the
042   * current period (auto or teleop). Warning: This is not an official time (so it cannot be used to
043   * dispute ref calls or guarantee that a function will trigger before the match ends).
044   *
045   * <p>When connected to the real field, this number only changes in full integer increments, and
046   * always counts down.
047   *
048   * <p>When the DS is in practice mode, this number is a floating point number, and counts down.
049   *
050   * <p>When the DS is in teleop or autonomous mode, this number returns -1.0.
051   *
052   * <p>Simulation matches DS behavior without an FMS connected.
053   *
054   * @return Time remaining in current match period (auto or teleop) in seconds
055   */
056  public static double getMatchTime() {
057    return MatchState.getMatchTime();
058  }
059
060  /**
061   * Pause the execution of the thread for a specified period of time. Motors will continue to run
062   * at their last assigned values, and sensors will continue to update. Only the task containing
063   * the wait will pause until the wait time is expired.
064   *
065   * @param period Length of time to pause
066   */
067  public static void delay(final Time period) {
068    delay(period.in(Seconds));
069  }
070
071  /**
072   * Pause the execution of the thread for a specified period of time given in seconds. Motors will
073   * continue to run at their last assigned values, and sensors will continue to update. Only the
074   * task containing the wait will pause until the wait time is expired.
075   *
076   * @param seconds Length of time to pause
077   */
078  public static void delay(final double seconds) {
079    try {
080      Thread.sleep((long) (seconds * 1e3));
081    } catch (final InterruptedException ex) {
082      Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
083    }
084  }
085
086  private long m_startTimeNs;
087  private double m_startTimeRemainderNs;
088  private double m_accumulatedTimeNs;
089  private boolean m_running;
090
091  /**
092   * Creates a new timer. The timer is initially not running and must be started with {@link
093   * #start()} to start measuring time. Consider using {@link #createStarted()} instead if the timer
094   * will be used immediately after creation.
095   */
096  public Timer() {
097    reset();
098  }
099
100  /**
101   * Creates a new timer that begins started.
102   *
103   * <p>This is equivalent to
104   *
105   * {@snippet lang="java":
106   *  Timer timer = new Timer();
107   *  timer.start();
108   * }
109   *
110   * @return A new started timer.
111   */
112  public static Timer createStarted() {
113    var timer = new Timer();
114    timer.start();
115    return timer;
116  }
117
118  private long getNsClock() {
119    return RobotController.getTime();
120  }
121
122  private double getNanoseconds() {
123    if (m_running) {
124      return getNsClock() - m_startTimeNs - m_startTimeRemainderNs + m_accumulatedTimeNs;
125    } else {
126      return m_accumulatedTimeNs;
127    }
128  }
129
130  /**
131   * Get the current time from the timer. If the clock is running it is derived from the current
132   * system clock the start time stored in the timer class. If the clock is not running, then return
133   * the time when it was last stopped.
134   *
135   * @return Current time value for this timer in seconds
136   */
137  public double get() {
138    return getNanoseconds() / 1_000_000_000.0;
139  }
140
141  /**
142   * Reset the timer by setting the time to 0.
143   *
144   * <p>Make the timer startTime the current time so new requests will be relative now.
145   */
146  public final void reset() {
147    m_accumulatedTimeNs = 0.0;
148    m_startTimeNs = getNsClock();
149    m_startTimeRemainderNs = 0.0;
150  }
151
152  /**
153   * Start the timer running. Just set the running flag to true indicating that all time requests
154   * should be relative to the system clock. Note that this method is a no-op if the timer is
155   * already running.
156   */
157  public void start() {
158    if (!m_running) {
159      m_startTimeNs = getNsClock();
160      m_startTimeRemainderNs = 0.0;
161      m_running = true;
162    }
163  }
164
165  /**
166   * Restart the timer by stopping the timer, if it is not already stopped, resetting the
167   * accumulated time, then starting the timer again. If you want an event to periodically reoccur
168   * at some time interval from the start time, consider using advanceIfElapsed() instead.
169   */
170  public void restart() {
171    if (m_running) {
172      stop();
173    }
174    reset();
175    start();
176  }
177
178  /**
179   * Stop the timer. This computes the time as of now and clears the running flag, causing all
180   * subsequent time requests to be read from the accumulated time rather than looking at the system
181   * clock.
182   */
183  public void stop() {
184    if (m_running) {
185      m_accumulatedTimeNs = getNanoseconds();
186      m_running = false;
187    }
188  }
189
190  /**
191   * Check if the period specified has passed.
192   *
193   * @param period The period to check.
194   * @return Whether the period has passed.
195   */
196  public boolean hasElapsed(Time period) {
197    return hasElapsed(period.in(Seconds));
198  }
199
200  /**
201   * Check if the period specified has passed.
202   *
203   * @param seconds The period to check in seconds.
204   * @return Whether the period has passed.
205   */
206  public boolean hasElapsed(double seconds) {
207    return getNanoseconds() >= seconds * 1e9;
208  }
209
210  /**
211   * Check if the period specified has passed and if it has, advance the start time by that period.
212   * This is useful to decide if it's time to do periodic work without drifting later by the time it
213   * took to get around to checking.
214   *
215   * @param seconds The period to check.
216   * @return Whether the period has passed.
217   */
218  public boolean advanceIfElapsed(double seconds) {
219    double periodNs = seconds * 1e9;
220
221    if (getNanoseconds() >= periodNs) {
222      // Advance the start time by the period.
223      // Don't set it to the current time... we want to avoid drift.
224      double advanceNs = m_startTimeRemainderNs + periodNs;
225      long wholeNs = (long) advanceNs;
226      m_startTimeNs += wholeNs;
227      m_startTimeRemainderNs = advanceNs - wholeNs;
228      return true;
229    } else {
230      return false;
231    }
232  }
233
234  /**
235   * Whether the timer is currently running.
236   *
237   * @return true if running.
238   */
239  public boolean isRunning() {
240    return m_running;
241  }
242}
